title: How balancing rocks stay perched
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How can a big rock balance on a tiny point?
What would make a balancing rock fall?

left.label: Rock's left side
left.ask: Why don't balancing rocks fall over?

explain.say: Balancing rocks are big boulders perched on a tiny point, often on top of other rocks. Many were left as wind, water and frost wore away the softer rock around them over thousands of years.

left.label: Rock's left side
left.ask: Why don't balancing rocks fall over?

explain.say: A rock balances when its centre of gravity sits right above the point it rests on. Then the weight on one side turns it one way exactly as much as the weight on the other side turns it back.

left.label: Rock's left side
left.ask: Why don't balancing rocks fall over?

explain.say: If the balance is upset, say a chunk breaks off one side, the turning effects no longer match. The heavier side wins and the rock topples.

right.label: Right side, chipped
right.ask: What would make a balancing rock fall?

explain.say: Fragile balancing rocks near faults are clues for scientists: if one has stood for thousands of years, the ground there can't have shaken hard enough to knock it over in that time.

faq.q: Why don't balancing rocks fall over?
faq.a: Their centre of gravity sits right above the spot where they touch the rock below. The weight on each side of that point turns the rock equally, so it stays put.
asks: How can a big rock balance on a small point?

faq.a: Most are left behind by weathering. Water seeps into cracks and wears away the rock around a harder core over thousands of years, leaving a boulder resting on a narrow base. Some were dropped by melting glaciers.
A moment is the turning effect of a force. It equals the force multiplied by its distance from the pivot, so a small weight far out can balance a big weight close in.

faq.q: What would make a balancing rock fall?
faq.a: Anything that moves its centre of gravity away from above its base: strong earthquake shaking, a chunk breaking off, or the ground under it wearing away. Then the turning effects no longer cancel and it topples.
asks: Can wind knock over a balancing rock?

faq.q: What can balancing rocks tell us about earthquakes?
faq.a: Delicately balanced rocks near faults would be knocked over by strong shaking. If one has stood for thousands of years, scientists know the ground nearby hasn't shaken that hard in that time, which helps them judge earthquake risk.
asks: Why do scientists study balancing rocks?

facts: An object balances when its centre of gravity is directly above its point of support.
Precariously balanced rocks near faults are used to check how strong past earthquake shaking could have been.

quiz.say: A balancing rock is perched on a point. A large chunk breaks off its left side. Which way does it tip?
quiz.show: A chunk breaks off the left side. The rock tips…
quiz.why: The right side is now heavier, so its turning effect wins and the rock tips towards the right.

wrong.0: The left side got lighter, so it can no longer hold the right side down.
wrong.2: Losing weight on one side upsets the balance.
